text:
sam: seeing repeated 95-99p latency spikes on perf-canary when medium requests (~40-70 tokens) mix with short ones. looks like path flipflop between prefill and decode kernels.

runtime-bot: alert perf-canary: 95p_latency increased +22% over baseline in last 10m (route: /generate, model: opt-6.7b-int8).

maria: confirmed in traces — kernel selection toggles every other request in some batches. KV cache hit patterns show partial misses due to interleaved seqlens.

ajay: autotuner currently uses a hard threshold at 48 tokens to pick prefill path on H100. when mixed batches contain both 30 and 55 tokens it picks prefill and we pay decode penalty for short ones.

sam: do we have profiler samples? can we see where time is going?

perf-bot: uploading sample profile (stacked) for canary run 2026-03-16_14:02:
```
Total requests: 1200
Avg tokens/request: 42
Kernel prefill path: 58% time
Kernel decode path: 22% time
KV serialization / eviction: 12% time
Other (IO, batching): 8%
95p latency: 312 ms (baseline 256 ms)
```

maria: KV eviction spikes align with when the batch switches ordering (shorts first vs longs first). looks like our KV cache compact/eject heuristic runs more aggressively when the runtime believes decode path will be used. that then causes the next request to miss and pick prefill kernel, flip again.

ajay: hypothesis: autotuner oscillates because metric it optimizes is instantaneous token throughput per kernel, without hysteresis or momentum. we should add a per-route smoothing window and a hysteresis band of +/-8 tokens before switching path. also consider tracking per-device kernel success ratio so arch-aware picks (A100 vs H100) use different thresholds.

jen: propose small canary change: add "kernel_hysteresis_tokens": 8 and "kernel_history_span": 120s to the autotuner config, plus per-gpu counters stored in runtime state. canary on staging first then prod small pct.

sam: sound good. what's the minimal patch?

ajay: two defs and a flag:
1) add TokenHysteresis to seqlen bucketer (int)
2) expose per-gpu kernel_history: map<kernel_name,int> (persist in local shm)
3) feature flag: runtime.autotune.kernel_hysteresis=true

jen: i'll draft the PR. test plan:
- unit: hysteresis logic for boundary cases (47,48,55)
- integration: run mixed seqlen replay for 1h on staging canary (10%)
- perf: measure 95p and kernel flip rate (target: flip rate < 1 per 1000 reqs)

sam: also add a short cooldown after a kernel change (e.g., 5s) to avoid thrash under bursty traffic.

maria: note: for KV cache, add metrics: kv_eviction_count_by_seqlen_bucket and kv_miss_rate_by_kernel so we can correlate. can we emit those from the canary?

perf-bot: canary results (staging 10% with hysteresis + cooldown) after 2h:
```
flip_rate: 0.9 -> 0.08 per 1000 reqs
95p latency: 312 ms -> 268 ms
KV eviction rate: -40%
overall cost delta: -1.8% token-equivalent
```

ajay: nice. but saw one regression on older A100 fleet where prefill kernel was still selected too often for 44-46 range. likely arch-specific kernel perf differences. we should make thresholds per-arch and fall back to global if missing.

jen: action items:
- jen: open PR with config + unit tests (ETA: today EOD)
- ajay: add per-arch thresholds and GPU-history counters to runtime (ETA: 2 days)
- maria: add KV metrics to exporter and dashboard (ETA: 1 day)
- sam: canary rollout and monitor 95/99p, flip_rate, kv_evictions (ETA: after PR merged)

sam: assigned. we'll reconvene tomorrow after first prod canary ramp. thanks all :thumbsup:

runtime-bot: note: generating audit event for config change: feature_flag kernel_hysteresis scheduled for canary rollout by sam.

maria: one more thought — let's keep a lightweight trace sampling for any kernel switch events with full KV map snapshot to debug future weirdness. small perf cost but worth it for postmortems.

ajay: agreed. will add sampling at 0.1% for kernel switch traces.

sam: perfect. closing the thread; will ping when canary starts.
